checked.note: Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit method signatures for the asset API serializer fields, assignment display, and checkout validation boundary. Serializer behavior, model fields, and ORM access remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.

Issue #613 admission: the specification read-transport scalars (SafeInteger, Decimal, Date, the opaque revision and cursor, and JSON) rewritten for the Strawberry port. Coercion is pure transport validation over the shared codec envelope and touches no ORM state.

Issue #446 bounded model-support admission: the pure depreciation policy resolver and book-value calculation contract. The implementation remains ORM-free and preserves disposal freezing, threshold ordering, schedule conventions, salvage floors, and rounding; private arithmetic helpers remain outside this admission.

Slice 7 symbol admission: the bulk check-in task entry envelope and its date parser -- the Job id, the asset pk list, the acting user/tenant, the optional status/location overrides, the check-in date, and the notes a scanner submits, plus the implicit None outcome the worker reports. Asset pks and status/location ids stay int | str because the enqueuing view forwards raw POST values; the ORM lookups, the checkin_asset service call, and the notification bodies remain outside this slice.

Slice 7 symbol admission: the bulk checkout task entry envelope and its date parser -- the Job id, the asset pk list, the target discriminator and target pk, the acting user/tenant, notes, optional status override, and the expected-check-in/checkout dates, plus the implicit None outcome. Target and status ids stay int | str because the enqueuing view forwards raw POST values; ContentType resolution, row locking, and the checkout_asset service call remain outside this slice.

Slice 8 symbol admission: the nightly depreciation materialisation task entry point -- no arguments, and the count of assets whose book value actually changed as int. The cross-tenant asset query, compute_book_value, and the bulk_update write remain outside this slice.

Slice 7 symbol admission: the bulk disposal task entry envelope and its two pure parsers -- the Job id, the asset pk list, the acting user/tenant, the shared disposal payload, and the per-asset proceeds map, plus the implicit None outcome. Both JSON-ish maps are declared as Mapping[str, object] because they arrive as a serialised task payload; _parse_proceeds therefore takes object and answers a non-negative Decimal or None. Narrowing the payload values, the already-disposed skip rule, and the dispose_asset service call remain outside this slice.

Slice 10 symbol admission: the Intune discovery task's named Graph payload and persisted result contracts and its task/service boundaries. IntuneDevicePayload and IntuneAppPayload describe the selected string fields consumed from the external Graph JSON; IntuneSyncResult fixes the seven integer count keys Job.result stores after a run; tenant, asset, and service internals remain outside the projection.

Slice 7 symbol admission, narrowed when the label engine became generic: this module is now only the queue-compatibility entry that delegates a job queued under the former asset-only task path to extras.tasks.labels. The moved helpers and the generic task continue under sequences 78 and 79.

Issue #446 bounded public service admission: typed audit result contracts and explicit actor/system authorization boundaries for expected-set, classification, basket commit, frozen-report read, close, rehome, and flag operations. Private ORM/query/parser internals remain outside the projection; the existing SystemAuthorizationContext contract is reused unchanged.
Issue #454 admission: typed verified identity value object, resolver protocol, canonical Phase-A/Phase-B handoff, and parameterized PostgreSQL timeout/lock boundaries.
Slice 1 symbol admission: SystemAuthorizationContext contract value object and validation signature; surrounding request-context helpers remain outside this slice.

Issue #613 admission: the shared BigInt/JSONString transport scalars introduced by the Graphene-to-Strawberry port, keeping the previous wire contract. The module depends only on strawberry and graphql.
Issue #443 admission: SDK-free identity provisioning command/result boundary and operation-time typed provider dispatch.
Issue #454 admission: configured issuer resolution and strict operator identity input boundary.
Issue #454 admission: shared ObjectChange writer preserves truthful actor and tenant semantics while applying scoped representation redaction.
Issue #454 admission: whole identity validation, lock framing, context-safe audit redaction, and profile audit payload module.
Public domain-blind single-provider lifecycle primitive with identity-safe registration and ContextVar-local overrides.

Slice 11 symbol admission: the immutable report request/result value objects and the ReportDefinition provider contract, including tenant scope, row/summary/chart hooks, and sample fallback signatures. Domain provider bodies and ORM implementations remain outside this projection.

Slice 11 symbol admission: report scope resolution, common row grouping, and the six-part build_report_context return boundary. Permission checks, provider dispatch, and historical context assembly behavior remain unchanged.

Slice 11 symbol admission: the report-provider registration, lazy discovery, typed lookup, and registered-identifier boundaries. Duplicate detection, discovery locking, and missing-provider failures remain unchanged.
Issue #443 admission: SDK-free restore-authority port, fail-closed dispatch, and operation-time provider override boundary.

Slice 3 symbol admission: the TaskContext background-task scope manager -- its constructor, entry/exit protocol, captured-context attributes, principal/tenant resolution, and the system-authorization issuing signature. The surrounding task helpers in core.tasks.* and every task payload they carry remain outside this slice.

Slice 8 symbol admission: the CSV/YAML bulk-import task entry envelope -- the Job id, the parsed rows the enqueuing view stored in the session, the target app_label/model_name pair, the acting user/tenant, and the implicit None outcome. Rows are Sequence[Mapping[str, object]] because they arrive as a serialised task payload of parsed cells; the dynamic BulkImportForm resolution, its import_data contract, and the notification bodies remain outside this slice.

Slice 8 symbol admission: the tenant LDAP directory-sync task entry envelope -- the Job id, the tenant slug the management command is invoked for, the acting user/tenant, and the implicit None outcome. The JobLogStream adapter that pipes command output into the Job log, the call_command invocation, and the notification bodies remain outside this slice.

Slice 8 symbol admission: the scheduled changelog-prune task entry point -- no arguments and the implicit None outcome, with exceptions still propagating so django-q2 records a Failure row. The prune_changelog management command it delegates to remains outside this slice.
Slice 8 symbol admission: the shared job-detail URL helper every task notification uses -- a Job id in, a URL string out, including the hand-built fallback path when reverse() fails.
Typed, domain-blind tenant access protocol and one explicit provider-slot port for framework and kernel callers.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit method signatures for webhook URL validation, event vocabulary validation, notification representation/config handling, and journal validation. Existing security and tenant-boundary behavior remains unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.

Continues the sequence 69 admission for the generic label engine: the authored print CSS loader, the bounded CSS measurement helper, the generic chunk_list pager and the data-URI barcode producer, now typed over the admitted LabelContent DTO (and its LabelNotApplicable refusal) instead of an asset. The Jinja2 sandbox, the card renderers and the xhtml2pdf emitters remain outside this slice.

Slice 8 symbol admission: the two alert-evaluation task entry points -- the scheduled sweep over every active rule and the single-rule 'Run now' action, both answering the count of freshly triggered alerts as int, and the AlertRule pk the action is handed. Rule matching, the open-log dedup prefetch, channel dispatch, and auto-resolution helpers remain outside this slice.
Continues the sequence 69 admission for the generic queued label task entry envelope (any labelled model, persisted tenant scope).

Slice 4 symbol admission: the _ReportOutput scheduled-report result contract -- the rendered email body plus the optional attachment content, filename, and MIME type a renderer hands to the archive and delivery steps. Slice 5 adds generate_scheduled_report_task, the scheduled-report task entry envelope: the ScheduledReport id a worker is handed, and the bool | None outcome it reports back -- True or False for a report that was processed, None for a schedule with no resolvable tenant scope. The renderer and helper functions between the two, and the report-provider architecture behind build_report_context, remain outside this slice; report-provider contracts stay owned by #83.

Issue #445 symbol admission: send_webhook_task accepts a WebhookDeliveryAssertions identity envelope plus attempt, actor_id, and request_id metadata, and returns a typed DeliveryResult. The locked durable WebhookDelivery row is the sole source of snapshotted target URL, method, headers, encrypted secret, event identity, tenant, payload timestamp, and retry policy; none of those values is accepted from queue kwargs. Transport construction, claim fencing, retry scheduling, and recovery coordination remain outside this symbol slice.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit method signatures for assignment availability create/update and accessory, consumable, and component category representations. Stock guards, transaction boundaries, and ORM behavior remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.

Issue #446 bounded model-support admission for the authorized stock-write guard and stock adjustment entry point. Private ORM locking, model resolution, and quantity helpers remain outside the projection.

Slice 10 AC14 admission: explicit DRF base serializer hook and OpenAPI display contracts. Framework inbound hooks use the documented DRF Any boundary; fields and representation results remain concrete.
Slice 10 AC14 admission: custom field conversion/representation and generic-FK validation contracts used by OpenAPI serializers. Parser-native inputs remain at the DRF Any boundary.
Slice 10 AC14 admission: generic-object conversion and ObjectChange SerializerMethodField return contracts.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit license validation and license-seat create/update method signatures. Seat-capacity, checkout, transfer, and audit behavior remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.

Slice 1 symbol admission: ResourceAccessDecision contract value object; surrounding tenant/RBAC access helpers remain outside this slice. Slice 7 adds the module's public access boundaries: the tenant-group topology walks, the shared-resource preselector, the canonical stock-access resolver and its facades, the tenant-operation authorization, the accessible-tenant memo with its clock-based expiry, and the tenant access report. Users, tenants, stock rows, and grants are typed as object (model classes as type[object]) so the projection admits no ORM implementation, and shared_resource_ids publishes Iterable[int] rather than its QuerySet; SystemAuthorizationContext is the already-admitted contract for actorless authorization. The private resolver, batch evidence, grant search, and RBAC helpers remain outside this slice.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit tenant and contact-assignment validation method signatures. Generic-target tenant isolation and superuser group restrictions remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.

Issue #443 admission: declaration validation for the presentation overlay. Whole-module admission is intentionally not claimed because frozen build_matrix_models lacks a return annotation; this minimal symbol scope is the canonical clean boundary.
Slice 10 organization-service admission: compatibility facade that re-exports the typed resource-access boundary without importing membership or rolegrant services.
Slice 10 organization-service admission: typed, field-mappable service-error contract. ValidationError compatibility and message-disclosure ordering remain unchanged.
Issue #443 admission: organization-owned interactive and LDAP directory identity provisioning transaction, lock, reconciliation, and sanitized logging boundary.

Slice 10 organization-service admission: typed membership intent/plan/result contracts and the public authorization, planning, identity, and write entry points. Private ORM orchestration remains outside the projection.

Slice 10 organization-service admission: generic QuerySet/model container-visibility boundaries. Generic model identity is preserved with a bounded TypeVar; authorization and filtering behavior remain unchanged.
Issue #443 admission: organization-owned restore label dispatch and grant-authority validation adapter.
Issue #443 admission: organization-owned role and group grant validation with preserved escalation messages and scope semantics.
Issue #443 admission: presentation-free semantic role permission target catalog and live permission-set construction.

Slice 10 organization-service admission: named grant specs/plans/validated-token/change/result contracts, query helpers, validation, assignability, and the validated-only write entry point. Private ORM/reconciliation bodies remain outside the projection.
Organization-owned typed tenant access adapter returning concrete live membership rows and delegating canonical access decisions.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit procurement display, validation, receive-payload, and action-boundary method signatures. Purchase-order lifecycle and quantity guards remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98. The nested supplier serializer now lives in assets.api.nested_serializers (issue #500), so its symbol admission was dropped with the local definition.

Slice 9 symbol admission: explicit subscription and subscription-assignment initialization, validation, representation, update, and assigned-object method signatures. Tenant scoping and lifecycle behavior remain unchanged; generated-schema validation remains owned by #98.
Slice 10 AC14 admission: explicit return contract for the compatibility serializer referenced directly by extend_schema(request=...).
Users-owned token authenticator and TokenAuth OpenAPI extension with typed helper seams preserving token validation and tenant binding.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMAuthenticatedPrincipal protocol and SCIMBearerTokenAuthentication DRF authentication contract -- a Request in, the minimal authenticated-principal/credential pair or None out, and the WWW-Authenticate scheme it advertises. The protocol avoids importing project model classes into the bounded projection; tenant resolution, token validation, IP allowlist, has_perm authorization, and write-flag checks inside the method bodies are unchanged and remain outside this slice. Slice 10 extends the same contract with SCIMBearerTokenAuthenticationScheme's explicit dict[str, str] OpenAPI security definition.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMQuery structural protocol plus every SCIM filter parser/helper function. The runtime values remain Django Q objects, but the checked signatures expose only their combinable query-expression algebra, so the projection does not import django.db.models or the application model graph. The parser functions read no request state and touch no ORM row; their bodies remain behaviorally unchanged.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the two SCIM identifier-boundary functions of the 1.x dual-read window -- identifier_lookup, which answers the model lookup for a legacy integer or opaque UUID identifier, and identifier_lookup_or_none, which answers None instead of raising for an invalid member identifier. Slice 10 extends this bounded contract with get_scim_object_or_404, preserving the concrete model type across a tenant-scoped QuerySet; the lookup body remains unchanged.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMAuthenticatedPrincipal protocol and SCIMProviderBearerTokenAuthentication DRF authentication contract for the provider-level SCIM mount -- a Request in, the minimal authenticated-principal/credential pair or None out, over the managing (is_provider) tenant. The protocol avoids importing project model classes into the bounded projection; provider resolution, provider-token scoping, has_perm authorization, and write-flag enforcement inside the method bodies are unchanged and remain outside this slice.

Slice-0 pilot, hardened by Slice 2. Pure SCIM PATCH parsing: no ORM, no request state, no Django imports, so it is clean under the normative flags without depending on django-stubs model inference. Explicit Any values remain only at categorised external-JSON boundaries; absent patch fields use the typed _Unset sentinel.

Slice 12 symbol admission: the public SCIM provider mutation-service boundaries for user patches, group patches, group creation, uniqueness checks, persistence, and membership reconciliation. Private ORM helpers and endpoint views remain outside this projection; runtime mutation behavior is unchanged.

Slice 14 provider endpoint-view admission: the User and Group list/detail classes, including POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE contracts and class-visible helpers. Existing provider mutations, membership synchronization, response/error contracts, and runtime bodies remain unchanged.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMUserResource, _SCIMMembershipResource, and _SCIMGroupResource structural protocols plus the tenant- and provider-shared SCIMUserSerializer and SCIMGroupSerializer resource contracts. The schema-only nested serializers describe the User/Group JSON boundary used by the admitted return annotations. Selected fields and SerializerMethodField return signatures describe the SCIM User/Group JSON boundary without importing application model classes into the bounded projection. The service-provider serializer, context helper, and surrounding ORM/mutation code remain outside this admission; serializer annotations are intended to improve later OpenAPI inference without claiming schema validation owned by #98.
Issue #454 admission: users-owned OIDCIdentity model validation, global binding semantics, and sanitized representation.
Issue #454 admission: User audit snapshot and redacted OIDC profile-event signal boundaries.
